# Krishiv configuration reference

<!-- @generated by `cargo xtask docs-config`; do not edit. -->

Keys under `krishiv.experimental.` are experimental and off by default. Spark aliases are accepted in place of the Krishiv key; other unknown `spark.*` keys produce a warning, unknown `krishiv.*` keys an error.

| Key | Type | Default | Scope | Settable by | Since | Spark alias | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `krishiv.access.external.endpoint` | string | (none) | cluster | startup | 0.3.0 |  | Server mode, provider `external`: the `krishiv.access.v1` policy service. An `https://` URI, a Unix socket `unix:/path`, or `http://` to a loopback IP address only (`127.0.0.1`, `[::1]`; not a name). Required when `krishiv.access.provider` lists `external`. |
| `krishiv.access.external.securables` | string | `data` | cluster | startup | 0.3.0 |  | Server mode, provider `external`: what the policy service decides, a comma-separated list. `data`: tables, views, columns, namespaces, functions, paths, secrets and connections. `system` (the server's own objects, `System(..)`) is refused until the admin API and UI guards ask the service too; the role matrix decides them. |
| `krishiv.access.external.timeout` | duration | `200ms` | cluster | startup | 0.3.0 |  | Server mode, provider `external`: the deadline of one call to the policy service. Past it, every pair the call carried is refused (fail closed). |
| `krishiv.access.external.token` | string | (none) | cluster | startup | 0.3.0 |  | Server mode, provider `external`: the bearer token sent to the policy service, as a secret reference (`env:NAME` or `file:/path`, as `krishiv.auth.tokens.*`), never a literal. Unset: no `authorization` header. |
| `krishiv.access.provider` | string | (none) | cluster | startup | 0.2.0 |  | Server mode: the access-policy provider that decides data securables (tables, views, columns, namespaces, functions, paths, secrets, connections). `grants`: `GRANT`/`REVOKE` decide them, and the role matrix keeps deciding the server's own objects; an admin passes every data check. `roles`: the role matrix decides everything. Unset: `grants` when authentication is configured, otherwise `roles`. `external`: the policy service of `krishiv.access.external.endpoint` decides them (`krishiv.access.v1`) and the role matrix keeps only the server's own objects, so a viewer may write when the service allows it; `roles+external` keeps the role matrix on data too. A `+`-separated list (`roles+external`) is an intersection: every listed provider that decides a securable must allow it, and one no listed provider decides is refused. `krishiv server` does not apply `grants` yet: there the unset default is `roles` and a list naming `grants` is refused at startup. `catalog` is refused until it is available. Path confinement (`krishiv.io.local.allowedRoots`, `krishiv.io.objectStore.allowedPrefixes`) applies first under every provider. |
| `krishiv.advisor.enabled` | bool | `true` | session | user | 0.3.0 |  | Compute advisor hints (spill, missing statistics, skew, runtime-filter opportunity, memory wait) for every finished query. They appear in `EXPLAIN ANALYZE`, in `system.queries.hints` and in the stored profile. Off: none is computed and the `hints` column is NULL. Hints never change a plan or a result. |
| `krishiv.advisor.maxHints` | positive int | `32` | session | user | 0.3.0 |  | Most hints kept per query, in order; bounds the size of the `system.queries` row. |
| `krishiv.advisor.memoryWait.factor` | int | `1` | session | user | 0.3.0 |  | An operator raises a MEMORY_WAIT hint when its time blocked waiting for memory exceeds this multiple of its compute time (and `krishiv.advisor.memoryWait.minTime`). |
| `krishiv.advisor.memoryWait.minTime` | duration (bare number: ms) | `100ms` | session | user | 0.3.0 |  | Floor on the time an operator waited for memory before a MEMORY_WAIT hint is raised. |
| `krishiv.advisor.missingStats.minQError` | int | `4` | session | user | 0.3.0 |  | A table without statistics raises a MISSING_STATISTICS hint when the planner's row estimate for a join or aggregate input missed the actual rows by at least this factor (q-error). |
| `krishiv.advisor.missingStats.minRows` | int | `10000` | session | user | 0.3.0 |  | Floor on the larger of the estimated and the actual rows before a MISSING_STATISTICS hint is raised. |
| `krishiv.advisor.runtimeFilter.minDropPercent` | int | `50` | session | user | 0.3.0 |  | A hash join with an unfiltered key raises a RUNTIME_FILTER_OPPORTUNITY hint when it dropped at least this percentage of its probe rows (a lower bound: probe rows in minus rows out). |
| `krishiv.advisor.runtimeFilter.minProbeRows` | int | `1000000` | session | user | 0.3.0 |  | Floor on a hash join's probe rows before a RUNTIME_FILTER_OPPORTUNITY hint is raised. |
| `krishiv.advisor.skew.factor` | int | `4` | session | user | 0.3.0 |  | A key-partitioned operator raises a SKEW hint when its slowest driver did at least this multiple of the mean work of the other drivers (time, or rows when the row floor holds); at factor 4 that is 80% of the work at 2 drivers, 67% at 3 and 57% at 4. |
| `krishiv.advisor.skew.minRows` | int | `100000` | session | user | 0.3.0 |  | Floor on an operator's output rows for the row-based SKEW test. |
| `krishiv.advisor.skew.minTime` | duration (bare number: ms) | `200ms` | session | user | 0.3.0 |  | Floor on the slowest driver's compute time before a SKEW hint is raised. |
| `krishiv.advisor.spill.minBytes` | size | `64MB` | session | user | 0.3.0 |  | Floor on the bytes an operator wrote to disk before a SPILL hint is raised. |
| `krishiv.advisor.spill.minPercent` | int | `10` | session | user | 0.3.0 |  | An operator that spilled raises a SPILL hint when the bytes it wrote to disk are more than this percentage of the query's peak reserved memory (and at least `krishiv.advisor.spill.minBytes`). |
| `krishiv.agent.gateBytes` | size | `1GB` | session | admin | 0.1.0 |  | Agent mode (`krishiv sql --agent`, the REPL's agent output, MCP): a statement whose estimated table scans reach this many bytes is not run; the answer is the estimate and the plan outline, and the caller repeats it with `--allow-heavy` to run it anyway. A statement whose tables report no statistics runs. 0 turns the gate off. |
| `krishiv.cache.defaultStorageLevel` | enum (`NONE`, `DISK_ONLY`, `DISK_ONLY_2`, `DISK_ONLY_3`, `MEMORY_ONLY`, `MEMORY_ONLY_2`, `MEMORY_ONLY_SER`, `MEMORY_ONLY_SER_2`, `MEMORY_AND_DISK`, `MEMORY_AND_DISK_2`, `MEMORY_AND_DISK_SER`, `MEMORY_AND_DISK_SER_2`, `OFF_HEAP`) | `MEMORY_AND_DISK` | session | user | 0.2.0 | `spark.sql.defaultCacheStorageLevel` | The storage level `DataFrame.cache()`, `catalog.cacheTable` and `CACHE TABLE` use (`persist()` with no level too). Replication (`_2`, `_3`) is accepted and reported as asked; one copy is kept. |
| `krishiv.cache.maxBytes` | size | `512MB` | session | admin | 0.1.0 |  | Most bytes cached relations (`DataFrame.cache`, `persist`) may hold in memory, per session, as Arrow batches under the `relation_cache` memory pool. Materialization is lazy (on first use) and all-or-nothing: when caching a relation would exceed the cap, the query runs uncached instead of failing. `0` disables caching: queries always run uncached. |
| `krishiv.catalog.delegation.maxDistinctExchangesPerMinute` | positive int | `20` | cluster | startup | 0.2.0 |  | Most distinct sets of exchange claims (scope, audience, groups) a catalog with `auth = delegated` exchanges tokens for in one minute for one principal: the ceiling a client meets that varies its claims to get past `krishiv.catalog.delegation.maxExchangesPerMinute`. Past it a catalog call fails with `KRISHIV_CATALOG_LIMIT_EXCEEDED` until the minute is over. |
| `krishiv.catalog.delegation.maxExchangesPerMinute` | positive int | `60` | cluster | startup | 0.2.0 |  | Most RFC 8693 token exchanges a catalog with `auth = delegated` makes in one minute for one principal and one set of exchange claims (scope, audience, groups). An exchanged token is reused until it expires, so a client that sends a fresh token with the same claims on every call costs one exchange per exchanged-token lifetime. Past the limit a catalog call fails with `KRISHIV_CATALOG_LIMIT_EXCEEDED` until the minute is over. |
| `krishiv.catalog.maxColumns` | positive int | `10000` | cluster | startup | 0.2.0 |  | Most columns, nested fields included, of a table schema a lakehouse connector accepts from table metadata (a Delta `metaData` schema string, an Iceberg schema). A wider one fails the load with `KRISHIV_CATALOG_LIMIT_EXCEEDED`. |
| `krishiv.catalog.maxMetadataBytes` | size | `256MB` | cluster | startup | 0.2.0 |  | Largest piece of table metadata a lakehouse connector parses, counted on decompressed bytes: a catalog response, an Iceberg metadata file, a Delta commit file (`_delta_log/N.json`), `_last_checkpoint` or a `.crc` file, or a checkpoint's Parquet footer. A larger one fails the load with `KRISHIV_CATALOG_LIMIT_EXCEEDED` instead of being read. A legitimate Delta commit of about a million added files can pass the default; raise this key for such a table. |
| `krishiv.catalog.requestTimeout` | duration | `30s` | cluster | startup | 0.2.0 |  | Longest one request to an external catalog (Hive metastore, Unity Catalog, Iceberg REST) may take, connect and response included. A stalled catalog fails the call with `KRISHIV_CATALOG_FAILURE` naming the catalog. Redirects from a catalog are never followed. |
| `krishiv.catalog.vended.maxEntries` | positive int | `10000` | cluster | startup | 0.2.0 |  | Most vended credential answers the server keeps across all declared catalogs, one per caller identity and table. The limit counts answers, not credentials: one answer can hold a credential for each storage prefix of the table. The least recently used answer is dropped first and fetched again from the catalog on its next use. An expired entry is never used again, but it leaves memory only at the next lookup or insert of the cache: while no query uses a vended catalog, an expired credential can stay in memory. |
| `krishiv.catalog.vendedDefaultTtl` | duration | `15min` | cluster | startup | 0.2.0 |  | How long a storage credential vended by a catalog with `storage = vended` is used when the catalog gives no expiry for it (`s3.session-token-expires-at-ms`, `gcs.oauth2.token-expires-at`, `adls.sas-token-expires-at-ms.<host>`). After it the credential is fetched again from the catalog. A credential that stops working earlier is refreshed once and the request retried. A value below twice `krishiv.io.credentials.refreshSkew` is allowed: the credential is then refreshed after half its lifetime. Must be positive: `0s` refuses startup when a catalog has `storage = vended`. |
| `krishiv.checkpoint.dir` | string | (none) | session | user | 0.2.0 | `spark.checkpoint.dir` | The directory `DataFrame.checkpoint()` writes its snapshot under (Spark's `setCheckpointDir`). Unset: `checkpoint()` fails with `_LEGACY_ERROR_TEMP_3016`, `localCheckpoint()` needs no directory. Unlike Spark, the files are deleted when the checkpointed DataFrame and every frame derived from it are gone. |
| `krishiv.compute.id` | string | (none) | cluster | startup | 0.3.0 |  | The compute (cluster or warehouse) this engine runtime bills to. Every usage record in the query events carries it as `compute_id`. Unset, it is the host name. |
| `krishiv.connect.address` | string | `127.0.0.1` | cluster | startup | 0.3.0 | `spark.connect.grpc.binding.address` | The address the Spark Connect listener binds. Loopback by default (Spark binds every interface); a non-loopback address needs authentication configured, or the server refuses to start. |
| `krishiv.connect.artifacts.maxArtifactBytes` | size | `256MB` | cluster | startup | 0.3.0 |  | Most bytes of one Spark Connect artifact (`AddArtifacts`). A larger artifact is refused (`KRISHIV_ARTIFACT_LIMIT`, `RESOURCE_EXHAUSTED`) before its bytes past the cap are written; what was written is removed. |
| `krishiv.connect.artifacts.maxBytes` | size | `1GB` | cluster | startup | 0.3.0 |  | Most bytes of artifacts (`AddArtifacts`: Python files, archives, files and cached local relations) one Spark Connect session may hold, on disk and in memory together. A chunk that would pass it is refused before it is written (`KRISHIV_ARTIFACT_LIMIT`, `RESOURCE_EXHAUSTED`) and the artifact it belongs to is discarded. Released with the session. |
| `krishiv.connect.artifacts.maxTotalBytes` | size | `16GB` | cluster | startup | 0.3.0 |  | Most bytes of artifacts all Spark Connect sessions of the server may hold together, on disk and in memory (each session is also capped by `krishiv.connect.artifacts.maxBytes`). A chunk that would pass it is refused before it is written (`KRISHIV_ARTIFACT_LIMIT`, `RESOURCE_EXHAUSTED`). Must be at least `krishiv.connect.artifacts.maxArtifactBytes` (checked at startup). |
| `krishiv.connect.execute.abandonedTombstones` | int | `10000` | cluster | startup | 0.3.0 | `spark.connect.execute.manager.abandonedTombstonesSize` | How many abandoned operation ids are remembered, so reattaching to one answers `INVALID_HANDLE.OPERATION_ABANDONED`; the least recently used is forgotten first. |
| `krishiv.connect.execute.aheadBytes` | size | `64MB` | cluster | startup | 0.3.0 |  | Most bytes of encoded `ExecutePlan` responses one operation holds before its client reads them; past it the query pauses until the client catches up (the gRPC flow-control window is the backpressure), so no result is held in full. The bytes count against the memory pool. |
| `krishiv.connect.execute.detachedTimeout` | duration (bare number: ms) | `5min` | cluster | startup | 0.3.0 | `spark.connect.execute.manager.detachedTimeout` | A reattachable operation with no stream attached for this long is cancelled, removed and remembered as abandoned (reattaching then answers `INVALID_HANDLE.OPERATION_ABANDONED`). |
| `krishiv.connect.execute.maintenanceInterval` | duration (bare number: ms) | `30s` | cluster | startup | 0.3.0 | `spark.connect.execute.manager.maintenanceInterval` | How often the server looks for operations detached past `krishiv.connect.execute.detachedTimeout`. |
| `krishiv.connect.execute.retryBufferSize` | size | `10MB` | cluster | startup | 0.3.0 | `spark.connect.execute.reattachable.observerRetryBufferSize` | Bytes of already-sent `ExecutePlan` responses a reattachable operation keeps, newest first, so a client that lost its stream can reattach and resume; older ones are dropped. `0` keeps none. The bytes count against the memory pool. |
| `krishiv.connect.execute.senderMaxStreamDuration` | duration (bare number: ms) | `2min` | cluster | startup | 0.3.0 | `spark.connect.execute.reattachable.senderMaxStreamDuration` | After this long a reattachable `ExecutePlan` or `ReattachExecute` stream ends without `ResultComplete` and the client reattaches to continue. `0` never ends it. |
| `krishiv.connect.execute.senderMaxStreamSize` | size | `1GB` | cluster | startup | 0.3.0 | `spark.connect.execute.reattachable.senderMaxStreamSize` | After sending this many bytes (the response that crosses it is still sent) a reattachable stream ends without `ResultComplete` and the client reattaches to continue. `0` never ends it. |
| `krishiv.connect.handshakeTimeout` | duration | `10s` | cluster | startup | 0.3.0 |  | A new Spark Connect connection that sends no first byte for this long is closed, so silent sockets cannot hold `krishiv.connect.maxConnections` for longer; with TLS the whole handshake must also finish within it. `0s` means no deadline for either, so a client that stalls mid-handshake holds its connection slot until it disconnects. |
| `krishiv.connect.http2.maxConcurrentStreams` | positive int | `100` | cluster | startup | 0.3.0 |  | Most concurrent RPCs (HTTP/2 streams) on one Spark Connect connection; more are refused. |
| `krishiv.connect.http2.maxHeaderListBytes` | size | `16KB` | cluster | startup | 0.3.0 |  | The largest header list of a Spark Connect request. |
| `krishiv.connect.http2.maxPendingAcceptResets` | positive int | `20` | cluster | startup | 0.3.0 |  | Streams a client may open and reset before the server accepts them, before the connection is closed (the HTTP/2 rapid-reset bound). |
| `krishiv.connect.keepAlive.enabled` | bool | `true` | cluster | startup | 0.3.0 | `spark.connect.grpc.keepAlive.enabled` | Whether the server pings idle Spark Connect connections to find dead clients. |
| `krishiv.connect.keepAlive.time` | duration | `1min` | cluster | startup | 0.3.0 | `spark.connect.grpc.keepAlive.time` | How often the server pings an idle Spark Connect connection. |
| `krishiv.connect.keepAlive.timeout` | duration | `20s` | cluster | startup | 0.3.0 | `spark.connect.grpc.keepAlive.timeout` | How long the server waits for a keepalive answer before it closes the connection. |
| `krishiv.connect.maxConnections` | positive int | `1024` | cluster | startup | 0.3.0 |  | Most open Spark Connect connections; past it the server accepts no new one until one closes. |
| `krishiv.connect.maxInboundMessageSize` | size | `128MB` | cluster | startup | 0.3.0 | `spark.connect.grpc.maxInboundMessageSize` | The largest Spark Connect request message; a larger one is refused before it is read. |
| `krishiv.connect.maxOperationsPerSession` | positive int | `100` | cluster | startup | 0.3.0 |  | Most live Spark Connect operations (`ExecutePlan` calls not yet finished or released) of one session; a new one past it is refused with `KRISHIV_OPERATION_LIMIT`. |
| `krishiv.connect.maxPlanDepth` | positive int | `1024` | cluster | startup | 0.3.0 |  | Deepest message nesting a Spark Connect plan may have: a plan nested deeper is rejected while it is decoded, before anything recurses into it (Spark's default for `spark.connect.grpc.marshallerRecursionLimit` is also 1024). A relation or expression costs two levels, so the default allows about 500 chained operators. Values above 4096 are lowered to 4096, the most the decode stack is sized for. |
| `krishiv.connect.maxResponseBytes` | size | `1GB` | cluster | startup | 0.3.0 |  | Most bytes of encoded `ExecutePlan` responses all operations of the server may hold at once. Each operation reserves its worst case (`krishiv.connect.execute.aheadBytes` plus, reattachable, `krishiv.connect.execute.retryBufferSize`) before its first response and returns it when released, abandoned or ended; past the cap a new operation waits for one to end, a running one never waits. Must be at least that worst case (checked at startup). The reservation assumes responses smaller than the ahead budget: a reattachable operation can hold up to two responses more (the one being sent and the one crossing the retry window), each at most `spark.connect.grpc.arrow.maxBatchSize`; every held response is also reserved from the engine's memory pool, which stays the hard limit. |
| `krishiv.connect.maxSessions` | positive int | `1000` | cluster | startup | 0.3.0 |  | Most live Spark Connect sessions in the server; a new one past it is refused with `KRISHIV_SESSION_LIMIT`. |
| `krishiv.connect.maxSessionsPerPrincipal` | positive int | `100` | cluster | startup | 0.3.0 |  | Most live Spark Connect sessions of one principal; a new one past it is refused with `KRISHIV_SESSION_LIMIT`. |
| `krishiv.connect.port` | positive int | `15002` | cluster | startup | 0.3.0 | `spark.connect.grpc.binding.port` | The port `krishiv server` serves Spark Connect on (`sc://host:15002`). A port in use fails the start. |
| `krishiv.connect.pythonFunctions.catalog` | string | (none) | cluster | startup | 0.3.0 |  | Path of the SQLite catalog file that keeps the Python UDFs a client persists with the `krishiv.v1.PersistPythonFunction` command, per tenant: later sessions of the same tenant find them, also after a restart. Made when it is not there. Needs a `krishiv` binary built with the `python-function-catalog` feature; when unset, nothing is persisted and the command is refused. |
| `krishiv.connect.session.closedTombstones` | int | `1000` | cluster | startup | 0.3.0 | `spark.connect.session.manager.closedSessionsTombstonesSize` | How many released Spark Connect session ids are remembered, so reusing one answers `INVALID_HANDLE.SESSION_CLOSED`; the least recently used is forgotten first. |
| `krishiv.connect.session.idleTimeout` | duration | `1h` | cluster | startup | 0.3.0 |  | A Spark Connect session no RPC used for this long is released (its id then answers `INVALID_HANDLE.SESSION_CLOSED`); a session running a query is kept. `0s` never expires (Spark's `spark.connect.session.manager.defaultSessionTimeout`, whose `-1` this is). |
| `krishiv.connect.session.maintenanceInterval` | duration (bare number: ms) | `30s` | cluster | startup | 0.3.0 | `spark.connect.session.manager.maintenanceInterval` | How often the server looks for idle Spark Connect sessions to release. |
| `krishiv.delta.logThreads` | positive int | `4` | cluster | startup | 0.2.0 |  | Experimental. Threads of the one process-wide pool on which Delta log work runs (log replay, snapshots, commits, checkpoints): at most this many Delta kernel calls run at once across all queries, and a query waits for a free thread (a cancellable wait, measured by the `delta.log_pool.wait_ms` metric). Read when the pool first starts. |
| `krishiv.delta.maxCommitAttempts` | positive int | `10000000` | session | user | 0.2.0 | `spark.databricks.delta.maxCommitAttempts` | Most times a Delta write retries its commit after another writer committed first and no conflict was found: up to this many retries, so one more attempt in all, as delta-spark counts them. Past it the write fails with `DELTA_MAX_COMMIT_RETRIES_EXCEEDED`. |
| `krishiv.delta.snapshotCache.maxBytes` | size | `64MB` | cluster | startup | 0.2.0 |  | Experimental. Most bytes, estimated, the runtime's cache of Delta snapshots holds: each table's latest snapshot and its live-file listing, kept across queries so the next one reads only the newer log. The least recently used table leaves first; a table whose listing alone is larger keeps only its snapshot, and its files are listed again by each query. Read when the runtime starts. |
| `krishiv.deterministicOrder` | bool | `false` | session | user | 0.1.0 |  | Make a query's result reproducible, aiming at the same bytes at any thread count (a float sum under a window, a sort-merge join or a very large grouping can still differ, because those size their buckets by the thread count). A scan pipeline whose source can be split deterministically runs one driver per logical partition (up to 16), morsels are dealt to them by ordinal, and their partial states are combined in partition order, so partial states (a decimal `sum` or `avg`, whose overflow can depend on the order of the merges) merge the same way and a query without `ORDER BY` returns its rows in the same order on every run, byte for byte, for the engine's own scans. Any other pipeline (a sink that is not lane-safe, a source that reports no positions, a pushed `LIMIT`, an operator with work after its input, a memory limit under 4 GiB) runs on one driver. The key hashes take a fixed seed, so an operator that spills splits its rows the same way on every run. Costs parallelism where it falls back to one driver: meant for reproducing a result, comparing two builds, and tests. Memory pressure from other queries in the process can still change when an operator spills, or whether a hash join build copies its rows into blocks as they arrive, and so the order of what it returns. The branches of a `UNION ALL` under an operator that must see all of them (a hash join probing a union) take turns in branch order, so they lose their overlap too. Off by default. |
| `krishiv.events.file.maxBytes` | size | `256MB` | cluster | startup | 0.3.0 |  | Bytes after which the event file moves on to a new segment. |
| `krishiv.events.file.maxFiles` | positive int | `8` | cluster | startup | 0.3.0 |  | Event file segments kept; older ones are removed at rotation. |
| `krishiv.events.file.path` | string | (none) | cluster | startup | 0.3.0 |  | A path prefix for the JSON-lines event file: one event per line, schema `krishiv.event.v1`, rotated at `krishiv.events.file.maxBytes`. When unset, no file is written. |
| `krishiv.events.queueCapacity` | positive int | `10000` | cluster | startup | 0.3.0 |  | Events one event sink may hold waiting for its delivery thread. A full queue drops events (counted in the gauge `krishiv_events_dropped`) and never slows a query. |
| `krishiv.events.textMaxBytes` | size | `4KB` | cluster | startup | 0.3.0 |  | Most bytes of statement text a `submitted` event carries, cut at a character boundary. The text is always literal-masked first. |
| `krishiv.exec.agg.directKeys` | bool | `true` | session | user | 0.2.0 |  | Internal: a grouped aggregation whose key columns in a batch are all one-byte strings or small integers without NULLs finds each row's group through a table indexed by the packed key, and hashes only each new key's first row. Results are the same either way; false hashes every row. |
| `krishiv.exec.agg.distinctCountAtMerge` | bool | `true` | session | user | 0.2.0 |  | Internal: a grouped aggregation whose only DISTINCT aggregate is a count, beside at least one other aggregate, on more than one executor slot, runs one table of distinct (key, value) pairs with no payload and one table of the plain aggregates by key, and counts each pair where the pairs' tables merge, instead of a second hash aggregation over the pairs. Results are the same either way; false keeps the two aggregations in series. |
| `krishiv.exec.agg.outputFilter` | bool | `true` | session | user | 0.3.0 |  | Internal: a deterministic filter that reads only a grouped aggregate's values (a HAVING such as `sum(x) > 300`, through plain column projections) is also evaluated by the aggregate on each output batch's values before it decodes the keys, so only the groups that pass are decoded and handed on. The filter above still runs; results are the same either way. |
| `krishiv.exec.agg.rowLayout` | bool | `true` | session | user | 0.1.0 |  | Internal: grouped aggregations keep their keys as fixed-width rows in radix-partitioned tables and merge the partitions in parallel. Results are the same either way; aggregations with nested or dictionary keys keep the columnar path. |
| `krishiv.exec.batchSize` | int | `4096` | session | admin | 0.1.0 |  | Rows per batch passed between operators. Operators do about a millisecond of work per batch, so the scheduler can switch tasks between batches. |
| `krishiv.exec.coalesceInput` | bool | `true` | session | user | 0.3.0 |  | Internal: in a pipeline that ends in a hash join's build or an aggregation, the driver joins small batches (fewer than a quarter of `krishiv.exec.batchSize` rows, and of 4,096, as a selective filter or join leaves them) into batches of about `krishiv.exec.batchSize` rows before the build, the aggregation and a hash join's probe, so each pays its per-batch cost once per batch of that size. Rows keep their order, and only rows of one scan split are joined. The rows held are not charged to the query's memory, like any batch between two operators: each driver holds at most about one batch, and 1 MiB (or a 64th of the memory limit, if less), for each operator that joins its input. Results are the same either way. |
| `krishiv.exec.debug.planRoundTrip` | bool | `false` | session | admin | 0.1.0 |  | Internal, for tests: every query's physical plan is encoded to the `krishiv.plan.v1` wire format and decoded again before it runs, as a worker would receive it. A plan the format cannot carry, or one that decodes to a different plan, fails the query. Results are the same either way. |
| `krishiv.exec.join.buildProjection` | bool | `true` | session | user | 0.1.0 |  | Internal: an expression above an inner hash join that reads only the build input's columns, cannot raise and is narrower than the columns it frees is computed on the build input, so the hash table holds its result instead of those columns. Results are the same either way; false computes it above the join. |
| `krishiv.exec.join.buildSide` | bool | `true` | session | user | 0.1.0 |  | Internal: a semi, anti or left outer join whose right input is estimated much larger than its left builds its hash table from the left input (a right semi, right anti or right outer join). Results are the same either way; false keeps Spark's side (the right input). |
| `krishiv.exec.join.directIndex` | bool | `true` | session | user | 0.3.1 |  | Internal: a hash join build of at most 4,096 rows with one integer key whose values span at most four slots a row (at least 64 slots for a smaller build) is probed through an array indexed by the key, without encoding or hashing the probe keys (dimension joins such as TPC-DS q62's). A detailed profile (`PROFILE_DETAILED`) keeps the hashed probe, so it times that one. Results are the same either way; `false` keeps the hashed probe. |
| `krishiv.exec.join.fuseProbeSelect` | bool | `true` | session | user | 0.2.0 |  | Internal: a filter directly below a hash join's probe side, and a scan's runtime filters there, run inside the probe, which then joins the rows they keep without copying them first. Results are the same either way; turn it off to plan the filter as an operator of its own and keep the runtime filters in the scan. |
| `krishiv.exec.join.idleSpillAfter` | duration | `1s` | session | admin | 0.1.0 |  | How long a finished hash join build table may wait for its probe side to start before it counts as idle. When memory runs short, an idle table is spilled first, one partition at a time, before an operator that is running spills its own state; the probe reads the spilled partitions back from disk. A shorter wait keeps less memory idle; a longer one spills less often when the probe starts soon. |
| `krishiv.exec.join.radixBits` | int | `3` | session | user | 0.1.0 |  | Internal: a row-layout hash join build splits its rows into 2^bits partitions by the top bits of the key hash (3 to 6) and indexes them in parallel. Results are the same for every value. |
| `krishiv.exec.join.rowLayout` | bool | `true` | session | user | 0.1.0 |  | Internal: hash joins store their keys as fixed-width rows and index them with a table that switches by size between a flat and a salted directory. Results are the same either way; joins whose key types have no row encoding keep the columnar path. |
| `krishiv.exec.join.sharedBroadcastBytes` | size | `0B` | session | admin | 0.1.0 |  | Bytes the broadcast join tables one query shares among its tasks on a worker may hold; 0 sets no cap beyond the query's memory. A shared build that grows past it stops, and each task of the query builds its own table from the broadcast rows instead, spilling as needed. A cap below the query's memory avoids the spill of the query's other memory that precedes that fallback when the table does not fit. |
| `krishiv.exec.join.smj.bufferBytes` | size | `0B` | session | admin | 0.1.0 |  | Bytes of one join key's right-side rows a sort-merge join keeps in memory before it moves them to a spill file; 0 takes a share of the memory pool. Spark bounds these rows by count (`spark.sql.sortMergeJoinExec.buffer.in.memory.threshold` and `spark.sql.sortMergeJoinExec.buffer.spill.threshold`), which have no effect here. |
| `krishiv.exec.join.strategy` | enum (`auto`, `sortMerge`) | `auto` | session | user | 0.1.0 |  | Internal: `auto` runs equi-joins as hash joins unless a `MERGE` hint asks otherwise; `sortMerge` runs every equi-join without a strategy hint as a sort-merge join, except `NOT IN` and keys that cannot be ordered. Results are the same either way. |
| `krishiv.exec.lateFetch.maxRows` | int | `50` | session | admin | 0.1.0 |  | Most rows (limit plus offset) an ORDER BY ... LIMIT over a file scan may rank while reading only the sort keys and filter columns, fetching the other columns for the rows kept; 0 turns it off. Results are the same either way. |
| `krishiv.exec.scan.instanceProjection` | bool | `true` | session | user | 0.1.0 |  | Internal: a table the query reads more than once is one scan in the logical plan, whose columns are the union of what every reader needs. With this on, each instance under a projection, an aggregate or a join (through filters and aliases) reads only the columns that parent uses. Results are the same either way, except which CSV/JSON rows count as malformed (on follows Spark, which parses each instance's own columns); false reads the union in every instance. |
| `krishiv.exec.seed` | int | (none) | session | user | 0.1.0 |  | Internal, for tests: seeds the key hashes of grouped aggregations and joins and the order in which scan morsels are claimed, and runs aggregations in their deterministic mode, so that the order of groups and of unordered `LIMIT` rows is the same on every run. Unset, each query draws a random seed. |
| `krishiv.exec.sort.hashBuckets` | bool | `true` | session | user | 0.1.0 |  | Internal: the sort below a window with a PARTITION BY splits its rows into buckets by the hash of the partitioning keys and sorts, merges and evaluates the buckets in parallel. Results are the same either way. |
| `krishiv.exec.targetPartitionBytes` | size | `128MB` | session | admin | 0.1.0 |  | Target size of a partition for scans and exchanges. |
| `krishiv.experimental.groupKeyCodeForce` | bool | `false` | session | user | 0.2.0 |  | Experimental: apply `krishiv.optimizer.groupKeyCode` wherever an aggregate's shape qualifies, also when a key's distinct count is a guess or the estimated ratios say it does not pay. For measuring the rewrite; results are the same either way. |
| `krishiv.experimental.ivm` | bool | `false` | session | admin | 0.1.0 |  | Experimental: incremental maintenance of materialized views. |
| `krishiv.experimental.unalignedCheckpoints` | bool | `false` | cluster | startup | 0.1.0 |  | Experimental: allow unaligned checkpoints under sustained backpressure. |
| `krishiv.flightSql.enabled` | bool | `true` | cluster | startup | 0.3.0 |  | Whether `krishiv server` serves Arrow Flight SQL on its Spark Connect port, when the binary is built with the `flight-sql` feature. Off: the Flight SQL paths answer `UNIMPLEMENTED`. |
| `krishiv.flightSql.fetchIdleTimeout` | duration | `5min` | cluster | startup | 0.3.0 |  | How long an Arrow Flight SQL result stream may wait for its client to read the next message; past it the query is cancelled and the stream ends `DEADLINE_EXCEEDED` (`KRISHIV_FLIGHT_SQL_FETCH_IDLE`). Time the engine spends computing the next batch does not count. |
| `krishiv.flightSql.handleTtl` | duration | `10min` | cluster | startup | 0.3.0 |  | How long an Arrow Flight SQL statement or prepared-statement handle stays fetchable after its last use; its session's release ends it sooner. |
| `krishiv.flightSql.maxBatchRows` | positive int | `10000` | cluster | startup | 0.3.0 |  | The most parameter rows one Arrow Flight SQL prepared update binds; more is `INVALID_ARGUMENT`. |
| `krishiv.flightSql.maxCommandResultBytes` | size | `16MB` | cluster | startup | 0.3.0 |  | The largest result an Arrow Flight SQL command (a statement that is not a query, such as `SHOW TABLES`) may store for its ticket. The command runs once, at `GetFlightInfo`; a larger result is `KRISHIV_FLIGHT_SQL_RESULT_NOT_STORED`, which says the statement ran. |
| `krishiv.flightSql.maxHandleBytesPerPrincipal` | size | `64MB` | cluster | startup | 0.3.0 |  | The most bytes (SQL text, bound literals, schemas and stored command results) one principal's Arrow Flight SQL handles hold; past it the principal's oldest idle statement tickets are released, and a new handle is `KRISHIV_FLIGHT_SQL_HANDLE_LIMIT` when none is idle. |
| `krishiv.flightSql.maxHandlesPerPrincipal` | positive int | `1024` | cluster | startup | 0.3.0 |  | The most Arrow Flight SQL handles one principal holds across its sessions; past it a new one is `KRISHIV_FLIGHT_SQL_HANDLE_LIMIT`. |
| `krishiv.flightSql.maxHandlesPerSession` | positive int | `64` | cluster | startup | 0.3.0 |  | The most Arrow Flight SQL handles (statements and prepared statements) one session holds; past it a new one is `KRISHIV_FLIGHT_SQL_HANDLE_LIMIT`. |
| `krishiv.flightSql.maxSchemaTables` | positive int | `1000` | cluster | startup | 0.3.0 |  | The most tables an Arrow Flight SQL `GetTables` with `include_schema` loads schemas for; a listing over it is `INVALID_ARGUMENT` (narrow the pattern). |
| `krishiv.flightSql.maxStatementBytes` | size | `1MB` | cluster | startup | 0.3.0 |  | The longest SQL text an Arrow Flight SQL statement may have; a longer one is `INVALID_ARGUMENT` (`KRISHIV_FLIGHT_SQL_STATEMENT_TOO_LARGE`) before it is parsed. |
| `krishiv.flightSql.metadataTimeout` | duration | `1min` | cluster | startup | 0.3.0 |  | The time limit of one Arrow Flight SQL metadata listing (`GetTables` and the others); past it the call is `DEADLINE_EXCEEDED`. |
| `krishiv.flightSql.provisionalTtl` | duration | `1min` | cluster | startup | 0.3.0 |  | How long an Arrow Flight SQL session made for a call without a session cookie lives after its last call, unless a later call depends on its state (`SetSessionOptions`, a prepared statement, a `SET`/`USE`-class statement), in which case it lives as a cookie session does. A fetched cookie-less ticket ends its session at once. |
| `krishiv.history.literals` | enum (`keep`, `mask`) | `mask` | cluster | startup | 0.3.0 |  | `mask` (the default) replaces every string and number literal with `?` in the statement text and in the plan lines of the profiles stored under `krishiv.history.path`, so a stored profile carries no data values. `keep` stores them as `EXPLAIN ANALYZE` prints them. Credentials in a statement are redacted either way. |
| `krishiv.history.maxBytes` | size | `256MB` | cluster | startup | 0.3.0 |  | Most bytes the profile history under `krishiv.history.path` keeps. When a new file takes the store past this, the oldest files go first, so the newest queries stay. |
| `krishiv.history.path` | string | (none) | cluster | startup | 0.3.0 |  | A directory where the engine keeps one compact profile for every finished query, as Parquet files, so `system.queries` history survives a restart and a stored profile can be opened later. A profile has the plan, the operators' counters and the query's identity, and no result data; literals are masked unless `krishiv.history.literals` is `keep`. Every query that reached execution is stored, as the engine metrics count them: a statement refused in parsing, analysis or an access check is not. Writing happens after the result stream ends and never fails the query; a failed write is counted in `krishiv_history_write_failures`. When unset, nothing is stored. |
| `krishiv.iceberg.commit.maxIntervening` | positive int | `1000` | session | user | 0.3.0 |  | Most snapshots committed to a branch between the snapshot an Iceberg write (an INSERT OVERWRITE, delete, update or merge) started from and the branch's current head that its commit validates for conflicts. An INSERT OVERWRITE validates only under the write option isolation-level, and without validate-from-snapshot-id it validates the whole history, which counts here. A commit that finds more fails with KRISHIV_ICEBERG_COMMIT_CONFLICT rather than validating part of the history; appends validate nothing and ignore it. Read when the write is planned. Krishiv has no catalog that commits Iceberg overwrites, deletes, updates or merges yet, so until it runs them this has no effect. |
| `krishiv.iceberg.manifestCache.bytes` | size | `64MB` | cluster | startup | 0.2.0 |  | Estimated bytes of decoded Iceberg manifest entries kept in memory, least recently used first out, so that planning a snapshot again (a self-join, a CTE, the next query on the same table) does not fetch and parse its manifests again. Manifests are immutable, so entries are keyed by path and length and never go stale. One cache per Iceberg storage registration, shared by every table opened through it; 0 disables it. |
| `krishiv.iceberg.write.maxOpenFiles` | positive int | `100` | session | user | 0.2.0 |  | Most data files one Iceberg write task (one driver of an append) keeps open at once, one per partition it is writing. Past the cap the oldest-opened file is closed, and a partition seen again after its file closed gets a new file, so a write over more partitions per task than this writes more, smaller files. Read when the write is planned. |
| `krishiv.iceberg.write.statistics.enabled` | bool | `false` | session | user | 0.3.0 |  | Whether an append into an Iceberg table (`INSERT`, CTAS) also writes a distinct-count sketch (`apache-datasketches-theta-v1`) of each of its first 100 top-level primitive columns (not `uuid`) into a Puffin statistics file, committed with the snapshot in the same request, so the optimizer and other engines read the table's distinct counts without a scan. A snapshot gets statistics only when every row it holds is sketched: the table was empty, or the previous snapshot has statistics of the column; otherwise the column, or the whole file, is left out. Statistics never fail a write: on any failure, or a catalog refusing the update, the write commits without them. A table opts out with the table property `krishiv.write.statistics.enabled=false`. Off by default until the write cost of the sketches is measured. Read when the write is planned. |
| `krishiv.io.blockingThreads` | positive int | `8` | cluster | startup | 0.1.0 |  | Most blocking threads of the I/O runtime, where local-file reads and writes run: at most this many local-file requests run at once per executor (`krishiv.io.maxConcurrentRequests` still bounds those in flight). Each such thread keeps freed read buffers in its own allocator cache, so the bound also bounds that memory. Read when the session starts its executor. |
| `krishiv.io.cache.blockBytes` | size | `1MB` | cluster | startup | 0.1.0 |  | Size of the aligned blocks the cache stores and fetches; a read is served from the blocks it overlaps. |
| `krishiv.io.cache.diskBytes` | size | `10GB` | cluster | startup | 0.1.0 |  | Size cap of the block cache's disk part; the least recently used blocks are removed to stay under it (it may exceed the cap by one block while a block is written). |
| `krishiv.io.cache.enabled` | bool | `false` | cluster | startup | 0.1.0 |  | Cache the byte ranges read from remote object stores (data pages, footers and page indexes alike) in aligned blocks on local disk, with a small in-memory tier in front. A block is keyed by the store, the path, the object's version (ETag or modification time) and the block index, so an overwritten object never serves old bytes. The disk part starts empty and is removed when the session ends. Any cache failure falls back to the store. Local files are never cached. |
| `krishiv.io.cache.memoryBytes` | size | `64MB` | cluster | startup | 0.1.0 |  | Size of the block cache's in-memory tier (least recently used blocks). `0` keeps blocks on disk only. |
| `krishiv.io.cache.path` | string | (none) | cluster | startup | 0.1.0 |  | Directory of the block cache's disk part (a local SSD). Each cache uses a subdirectory of its own, empties it when created and removes it when dropped; subdirectories no running cache holds any longer are removed too. When unset: `krishiv-block-cache-<uid>` under the system temp directory (a directory this user does not own is refused). |
| `krishiv.io.coalesceBytes` | size | `1MB` | cluster | startup | 0.1.0 |  | Byte ranges of one file closer than this are fetched with one request, as long as the request reads few enough bytes outside the ranges (`krishiv.io.coalesceWasteBytes`, `krishiv.io.coalesceWasteDivisor`). |
| `krishiv.io.coalesceWasteBytes` | size | (none) | cluster | startup | 0.1.0 |  | Bytes outside the requested ranges that any coalesced read may fetch (besides `krishiv.io.coalesceWasteDivisor`'s share). A read's whole span is reserved while it is in flight, so this trades bytes read for fewer requests. When unset: 64 KiB for local files, 1 MiB for object stores and HTTP, where a request costs latency. |
| `krishiv.io.coalesceWasteDivisor` | positive int | `16` | cluster | startup | 0.1.0 |  | A coalesced read may fetch up to 1/this of its bytes outside the requested ranges (or `krishiv.io.coalesceWasteBytes`, whichever is larger). |
| `krishiv.io.credentials.refreshSkew` | duration | `5min` | cluster | startup | 0.1.0 |  | How long before its expiry a short-lived object-store credential (vended by a catalog or a token service) is refreshed. A request that arrives inside this window fetches a new credential first; an expired credential is never used. `0s` refreshes only at expiry. |
| `krishiv.io.egress.allowedCidrs` | string | (none) | cluster | startup | 0.2.0 |  | A comma-separated list of networks (`10.20.0.0/16`, `fd12:3456::/48`) the egress policy always allows, for every client. The only way to open a link-local address. Unset: none. |
| `krishiv.io.egress.privateAddresses` | enum (`allow`, `deny`) | (none) | cluster | startup | 0.2.0 |  | Whether the server's outbound connections for catalogs and data (catalog APIs, token endpoints, object-store requests, metastore connections) may reach addresses that are not globally routable. `deny` (the server-mode default when unset) allows only globally routable unicast addresses (IANA special-purpose registries), the networks of `krishiv.io.egress.allowedCidrs`, and private (RFC 1918, unique-local) or loopback addresses of a host an administrator declared, by its exact name and only for the client that owns it; link-local addresses (cloud metadata) never pass by name. The rule is checked after DNS resolution and on every redirect hop. Under `deny`, in server and embedded mode alike, certificate verification stays on: a store option that turns it off is refused. `allow` (the embedded default) applies no rule. |
| `krishiv.io.egress.proxy` | string | (none) | cluster | startup | 0.2.0 |  | An HTTP(S) proxy URL every egress-policy client sends through; the proxy then decides where requests may go (logged at startup). Unset: the policy clients use no proxy, environment proxy variables included. |
| `krishiv.io.footerReadBytes` | size | `64KB` | cluster | startup | 0.1.0 |  | Size of the speculative read at the end of a file that fetches its footer in one request; a format may ask for more (up to 1 MiB). |
| `krishiv.io.lateMaterialization` | enum (`auto`, `on`, `off`) | `auto` | session | user | 0.1.0 |  | Whether a Parquet scan evaluates its pushed filter on the filter's columns before decoding the others for the rows that pass: `auto` decides per row group from the fraction of rows the filter kept before, `on` and `off` force it. Returned rows are the same either way; with the filter, decode errors confined to rows it rejects (a corrupt page or invalid UTF-8 in a column it does not read) are not raised. |
| `krishiv.io.local.allowedRoots` | string | (none) | cluster | startup | 0.2.0 |  | Server mode (authentication configured): a comma-separated list of absolute paths of existing local directories (a path holding a comma cannot be listed) that reads and writes by path may use, for every role, admin included. A path is compared after `.`, `..` and symbolic links are resolved, and a glob or directory read below a root fails at a link out of every root. Unset or empty: no local path is allowed in server mode. Embedded use is not confined by path; set there, the key only makes listings refuse links out of the roots. |
| `krishiv.io.maxConcurrentRequests` | int | `64` | cluster | startup | 0.1.0 |  | Most object-store requests in flight at once per store, over all queries of the process. The local file store also runs each request on a blocking thread of the I/O runtime, so at most `krishiv.io.blockingThreads` of them run at once. |
| `krishiv.io.maxRequestBytes` | size | `16MB` | cluster | startup | 0.1.0 |  | Ranges are not coalesced into requests larger than this (a single larger range is still fetched whole). |
| `krishiv.io.maxRetries` | int | `5` | cluster | startup | 0.1.0 |  | Retries of an object-store request that failed transiently (throttling, unavailable, timeout), with jittered exponential backoff honouring `Retry-After`. |
| `krishiv.io.metadataCacheBytes` | size | `64MB` | cluster | startup | 0.1.0 |  | Size of the in-memory cache of decoded file footers and metadata (least recently used entries are evicted). `0` disables it. |
| `krishiv.io.multipartPartBytes` | size | `8MB` | cluster | startup | 0.1.0 |  | Part size of multipart uploads (at least 5 MiB; doubled every 1,000 parts so a file never needs more than the 10,000 parts object stores allow). |
| `krishiv.io.objectStore.allowedPrefixes` | string | (none) | cluster | startup | 0.2.0 |  | Server mode (authentication configured) only: a comma-separated list of object-store prefixes (`s3://bucket/prefix`, `gs://bucket`, `abfss://container@account.dfs.core.windows.net/prefix`; an Azure prefix names its account host) that reads and writes by path may use, for every role, admin included. A prefix matches whole key segments (`s3://b/data` does not match `s3://b/data2`) and holds no glob character; `s3` and `s3a` name the same store; a path holding `%`, `?` or `#` is never allowed, so `?` globs are refused. It is the one opt-in for the server's own (ambient) credentials and for `http(s)://` locations, which are refused unless listed. Any `fs.*` store option but an inline access key, secret, token or SAS (so endpoints, regions, accounts, key files, the GCS key JSON and tuning keys alike), per read, on a table or set in a session, needs admin; a table's options stored by an admin are not asked about again when others read or insert. Unset or empty: no object-store path is allowed. Embedded use and a server without authentication do not read it. |
| `krishiv.io.parquet.bloomFilter.enabled` | bool | `true` | session | user | 0.1.0 |  | Whether a Parquet scan reads the stored Bloom filters of the row groups its statistics could not decide and skips a row group when a pushed equality or IN literal cannot be in it. Returned rows are the same either way: the filter only prunes, and a filter that fails a check is ignored. Files without Bloom filters pay nothing. |
| `krishiv.io.parquet.dictionaryFilter.enabled` | bool | `true` | session | user | 0.2.0 |  | Whether a Parquet scan reads the dictionary page of a column chunk whose data pages are all dictionary encoded, for the row groups its statistics could not decide, and skips a row group when the dictionary holds no literal of a pushed equality or IN. Returned rows are the same either way: the dictionary only prunes, and a page that fails a check is ignored. Dictionary pages above 16 MiB are not read. |
| `krishiv.io.parquet.pageIndex.enabled` | bool | `true` | session | user | 0.1.0 |  | Whether a Parquet scan reads the page index of the row groups its statistics could not decide and skips the pages the pushed filter rules out. Returned rows are the same either way: the index only prunes, and an index that fails a check is ignored. Files without a page index pay nothing. |
| `krishiv.io.prefetchBytes` | size | `64MB` | session | admin | 0.1.0 |  | Bytes a file scan may fetch ahead of decoding, per scan driver. Prefetched bytes are reserved from the query's memory pool and dropped first under memory pressure. |
| `krishiv.io.requestTimeout` | duration | `30s` | cluster | startup | 0.1.0 |  | Timeout of one object-store request attempt; a timed-out attempt is retried. |
| `krishiv.io.strictOptions` | bool | `false` | session | user | 0.1.0 |  | When true, a data source option that the format does not know is an error (`KRISHIV_UNKNOWN_FORMAT_OPTION`). When false (the default, as in Spark), it is ignored with a warning that suggests the closest known option. |
| `krishiv.memory.abortReleaseTimeout` | duration | `30s` | cluster | startup | 0.1.0 |  | How long a memory request waits for queries the arbitrator aborted to release their memory; aborted queries release at their next batch boundary. While their memory covers the request, no other query is aborted. The request fails after this time. |
| `krishiv.memory.limit` | size | (none) | cluster | startup | 0.1.0 |  | Memory available to query execution in this process: the limit of the root memory pool. Operators reserve memory before allocating and spill when the limit is reached. When unset: 80% of the effective memory limit (the tightest cgroup limit, else physical memory), or 2 GiB where that cannot be determined. A value above that effective limit is not honoured (the kernel would kill the process before the engine spills): the default is used instead, with a warning. |
| `krishiv.memory.reservationQuantum` | size | `1MB` | cluster | startup | 0.1.0 |  | Granularity of memory reservations: a consumer takes memory from its pools in steps of this size (at most 1/64 of the smallest pool limit above it), so small reservations rarely touch shared counters. Unused parts of a step are reclaimed before anything is spilled. `1b` disables rounding. |
| `krishiv.memory.residentGuard` | bool | `true` | cluster | startup | 0.1.0 |  | Whether the root memory pool keeps what the process holds beyond its reservations (allocator overhead, memory used without a reservation) within an allowance of 1/8 of the limit plus 64 MiB, by lowering the memory ordinary reservations may take so operators spill. It needs a resident-set probe from the program that owns the allocator: on Linux, the `krishiv` CLI and the Python module (builds with mimalloc, as shipped) install one at every limit, the bench runner when started with a limit below 4 GiB; on macOS and Windows, and elsewhere, the setting has no effect. In the Python module the resident set includes the Python program's own memory (its DataFrames, NumPy and Arrow data), so that memory lowers what queries may reserve. Spill I/O and arbitration rounds whose spills are exhausted are exempt from it. |
| `krishiv.memory.spillScratchReserve` | size | `512KB` | cluster | startup | 0.1.0 |  | Memory at the top of every limited memory pool (at most 1/8 of its limit) that only spill writers' scratch buffers may use, so a full pool can still fund the spill that frees it. Shared by every spill under the pool and released when each write ends. `0` disables it. |
| `krishiv.memory.spillWaitTimeout` | duration | `2s` | cluster | startup | 0.1.0 |  | How long the memory arbitrator waits for a consumer asked to spill to begin spilling before it gives up on it and aborts the query furthest above its fair share of memory. A spill that has begun is awaited to its end. |
| `krishiv.metrics.enabled` | bool | `false` | session | admin | 0.1.0 |  | When true, every query that reaches execution folds its metrics into the engine's metrics registry once, at query end (`Session::metrics`, `krishiv.metrics()`); when false the fold is skipped entirely. Engine gauges (memory, spill disk, metadata cache size, build info) are evaluated when the snapshot is read either way. |
| `krishiv.network.timeout` | duration | `2min` | cluster | startup | 0.1.0 | `spark.network.timeout` | Default timeout for network interactions between cluster processes. |
| `krishiv.optimizer.derivedKeysAbove` | bool | `true` | session | user | 0.2.0 |  | Internal. Let an aggregate that groups by a column and by expressions of it only (ClickBench q36's `ClientIP, ClientIP - 1, ClientIP - 2`) group by the column alone and compute the expressions from it above the aggregate, so the hash table holds one narrow key instead of several. Applies only to deterministic built-in expressions that cannot raise (or whose range statistics prove no overflow) over keys whose equality is identity. Results are the same either way. On since its timed A/B (ClickBench q36: 0.82x). |
| `krishiv.optimizer.discoverKeys` | bool | `true` | session | user | 0.2.0 |  | Internal. Let the session prove a file table's key columns unique by reading them once before the query runs, when `krishiv.optimizer.payloadAboveAggregate` needs that fact for a join over plain files (TPC-H q10's `customer`). The answer is cached per file version: a later query over the same files reads nothing. A count that runs out of time or memory, or fails, proves nothing and the plan stays as it was. Results are the same either way. On by default; set false to never read data before planning. |
| `krishiv.optimizer.discoverKeys.timeout` | duration | `1min` | session | user | 0.2.0 |  | The time one query's key counts (`krishiv.optimizer.discoverKeys`) may take together: its tables are counted in turn, each with what the ones before it left. A count that runs out of time proves nothing; it is tried again only by a query given more time. |
| `krishiv.optimizer.eagerAggregation` | bool | `true` | session | user | 0.1.0 |  | Run an aggregate's calls below a join and merge their states above it, when statistics show the join keeps most rows and the join keys group them well. Only calls whose result cannot depend on row order or raise on a row the join would drop are moved. Results are the same either way. |
| `krishiv.optimizer.groupKeyCode` | bool | `false` | session | user | 0.2.0 |  | Internal. Let an aggregate whose group keys include several columns of one dimension table (TPC-H q16's `p_brand, p_type, p_size`) group by one integer code made on the dimension's side, and read the columns back from the dimension's distinct values above the aggregate, so the joins below it carry the code instead of the columns. Applies only when statistics say it pays. Results are the same either way. Off by default (one coded dimension can cost more than it saves); `krishiv.optimizer.groupKeyCodeMultiDimension` codes only aggregates with keys of two or more dimensions. |
| `krishiv.optimizer.groupKeyCodeMultiDimension` | bool | `false` | session | user | 0.3.0 |  | Internal. With `krishiv.optimizer.groupKeyCode` off, still code the group keys of an aggregate whose keys come from two or more dimension tables that each qualify (TPC-DS q47's `item` and `store`), all of them in one pass; an aggregate with keys of one dimension is left as it is, and so are dimensions with more than 100,000 groups or inputs too small to pay. Has no effect when `krishiv.optimizer.groupKeyCode` is on. Results are the same either way. Off until its default is decided (TPC-DS q47, q57 about 0.8x wall; q24, q72 about 1.05x). |
| `krishiv.optimizer.joinCost` | enum (`rows`, `bytes`) | `rows` | session | user | 0.1.0 |  | What the join optimizer minimises when it orders a tree of inner joins, and which input of each join it builds. `rows`: the rows of the intermediate results; the input with fewer rows is built; when two orders cost the same rows (to a relative 1e-9), the one whose builds hold fewer bytes wins. `bytes`: each join's result rows times 48 bytes plus the bytes of its build input (rows times the estimated width of the columns still read, Spark's default size per type); the input with fewer rows is built unless it holds more than twice the other's bytes. Results are the same either way. |
| `krishiv.optimizer.joinDpLimit` | positive int | `10` | session | user | 0.1.0 |  | Most inputs of an inner-join tree the `dpsub` join enumerator plans exactly; larger trees are planned greedily. Values above 14 count as 14: the work grows as 3 to the power of the inputs. Results are the same either way. |
| `krishiv.optimizer.joinEnumerator` | enum (`dpsub`, `greedy`) | `dpsub` | session | user | 0.1.0 |  | How the join optimizer orders each tree of inner joins. `dpsub`: dynamic programming over every split of every subset of the inputs, for trees of at most `krishiv.optimizer.joinDpLimit` inputs, greedy above. `greedy`: always join the connected pair with the fewest result rows. Results are the same either way; for comparing plans and planning time. |
| `krishiv.optimizer.latePayloadJoin` | bool | `true` | session | user | 0.1.0 |  | Join a dimension's payload columns (such as a name read only by the aggregate on top) after the semi, anti and outer joins that never read them, and leave a semi join on the dimension's keys where the join was, so those joins build and probe narrower rows. Applies when statistics show the payload is wide and the dimension is the smaller side. Results are the same either way. |
| `krishiv.optimizer.ndvSampling.enabled` | bool | `true` | session | user | 0.1.0 |  | Before a query is optimized, count the distinct values of the file columns an equality or IN compares with values, when the files store no distinct count, from the first rows of the table's files. The count steers join ordering and build-side choice; results are the same either way. Samples are kept per file version. |
| `krishiv.optimizer.ndvSampling.rows` | positive int | `131072` | session | user | 0.1.0 |  | The most rows a distinct-value sample of a table reads, from its first files in order. A table no larger than this is counted exactly. |
| `krishiv.optimizer.ndvSampling.timeout` | duration | `5s` | session | user | 0.1.0 |  | The time one query's distinct-value samples may take together: its tables are sampled in turn, each with what the ones before it left. A table that runs out of time, or gets none, keeps its default estimates; EXPLAIN COST and EXPLAIN VERBOSE say which ("Distinct-Value Samples"). The row limit is what bounds a sample; this only guards against slow storage, so that how fast the machine is does not decide the plan. |
| `krishiv.optimizer.payloadAboveAggregate` | bool | `true` | session | user | 0.2.0 |  | Internal. Let an aggregate that groups by a dimension's key and its other columns (TPC-H q10's customer and nation columns) group by the joining key of the other side instead, and join the dimension above the aggregate, so the aggregate and the joins below it hold narrow rows. Applies only where the dimension's key is proven unique (the plan groups it, the table's statistics declare it, or a key count proved it: `krishiv.optimizer.discoverKeys`), no aggregate argument can raise or overflow, and statistics say the join keeps most rows. Results are the same either way. On by default (TPC-H q10: 0.75x at SF100, 0.59x at SF1000). |
| `krishiv.optimizer.preAggregateExpand` | bool | `true` | session | user | 0.3.0 |  | Where an aggregate reads an expansion (GROUP BY ROLLUP, CUBE and GROUPING SETS, and the rewrite of several DISTINCT calls), aggregate the input rows into their finest groups before each row is repeated once per projection, and merge those groups' states per projection. Only calls whose result cannot depend on row order are moved; it runs with krishiv.optimizer.eagerAggregation. Results are the same either way. |
| `krishiv.optimizer.preservedSideSemiJoin` | bool | `true` | session | user | 0.3.1 |  | Reduce the preserved side of a `LEFT` or `RIGHT OUTER JOIN` by a key-only semi join with a filtered input that an inner join above joins to that side only (TPC-DS q40, q80: sales joined to a filtered item or date range above `sales LEFT JOIN returns`), so the hash join can build the reduced side instead of the whole outer side. Only when statistics say the semi join keeps at most a quarter of the side. Results are the same either way, except that an ANSI error Spark raises on a row the join above drops (in the outer join's condition or a projection above it) is not raised; `false` turns it off. |
| `krishiv.optimizer.semiAntiJoinOrder` | bool | `true` | session | user | 0.1.0 |  | Run the `LEFT SEMI` and `LEFT ANTI` joins stacked over one input (`EXISTS` and `NOT EXISTS` subqueries of one block, TPC-H q21) in the order of their estimated survivors, fewest first, instead of the order of the text, when their conditions cannot raise, and only when every input is estimated from statistics. Results are the same either way; `false` turns it off. |
| `krishiv.optimizer.shareFilteredScans` | bool | `true` | session | user | 0.3.0 |  | Read a table once when two or more filters are its only readers (TPC-DS q28): the rows any of the filters keeps are stored, and each filter reads them. Only when statistics say the filters keep at most a quarter of the table, and no predicate can raise. The stored rows are charged to the query's memory and spill to disk under pressure. Needs `krishiv.sql.optimizer.shareCteInstances`. Results are the same either way; `false` turns it off. |
| `krishiv.optimizer.shareLiteralInstances` | bool | `true` | session | user | 0.3.1 |  | Internal. Compute a CTE read several times with a different literal on one of its group keys (TPC-DS q31's `d_qoy = 1`, `2`, `3`) once for all the literals (`d_qoy IN (1, 2, 3)`), each reader keeping the groups of its own literal. Needs `krishiv.sql.optimizer.shareCteInstances`. Results are the same either way; `false` turns it off. |
| `krishiv.optimizer.shareRepeatedSubtrees` | bool | `true` | session | user | 0.1.0 |  | Compute an uncorrelated subtree once when the main block reads it directly and a subquery reads it again (TPC-H q11), and let both read the stored result. Needs `krishiv.sql.optimizer.shareCteInstances`. Results are the same either way; `false` turns it off. |
| `krishiv.optimizer.subqueryAsWindow` | bool | `true` | session | user | 0.1.0 |  | Compute a correlated scalar aggregate subquery over the same relations and filters as the outer block (TPC-H q17, q02) as a window over the outer join's rows, so the big table is read once. Only `min`, `max` and exact decimal `avg` of non-floating, non-collated keys qualify, and only when statistics say the rewrite pays. Results are the same either way; `false` turns it off. |
| `krishiv.python.udf.threads` | int | `0` | cluster | startup | 0.1.0 |  | Threads of the embedded Python UDF pool, fixed when the pool starts (the first query calling a Python UDF). 0 picks one: the executor's thread count on a free-threaded Python, else 1 (with the GIL more threads only contend). A value of 1 starts two OS threads, so a scalar UDF call queued behind a relation task runs beside it; scalar calls still run one at a time. With two or more threads, one stays free for scalar UDFs, so a grouped-aggregate or map UDF relation can use at most threads - 1. |
| `krishiv.python.worker.executables` | string | `python3` | cluster | startup | 0.2.0 |  | Comma-separated Python interpreters the server's UDF workers may run (absolute paths, or names looked up on the server's `PATH` at startup). Each needs Python 3.11 or later with `pyspark-client` (or `pyspark`) of the clients' version, `pyarrow` and `pandas`. A worker runs the listed interpreter whose `major.minor` is the client's, else the first usable one. |
| `krishiv.python.worker.idleTimeout` | duration | `1min` | cluster | startup | 0.2.0 |  | How long an idle Python UDF worker is kept for the next task of its session before it is stopped. |
| `krishiv.python.worker.maxPerSession` | positive int | `8` | cluster | startup | 0.2.0 |  | Most Python UDF worker processes one session runs at once; further UDF calls wait for one of them. |
| `krishiv.python.worker.maxPerTenant` | positive int | `32` | cluster | startup | 0.3.0 |  | Most Python UDF worker processes one tenant runs at once, over all its sessions, and most calls it runs at once; further calls wait, so one tenant cannot take every worker or call thread. Sessions without a tenant count per principal; with authentication off there is no such cap. A tenant's workers are never shared with another tenant. |
| `krishiv.python.worker.maxTotal` | positive int | `64` | cluster | startup | 0.2.0 |  | Most Python UDF worker processes the server runs at once, over all sessions; at the limit an idle worker of another session is stopped, else the call waits. |
| `krishiv.python.worker.memoryLimit` | size | `1GB` | cluster | startup | 0.2.0 |  | Address-space limit of each Python UDF worker (`RLIMIT_AS`). A UDF that allocates past it gets a `MemoryError` or ends its worker; the server is not affected. |
| `krishiv.python.worker.sandbox.allowFork` | bool | `false` | cluster | startup | 0.2.0 |  | Lets sandboxed Python UDFs fork (`multiprocessing`, `os.fork`). The other layers stay: a forked process still cannot run other programs, open sockets or read files outside the allowed paths. Spark's workers may fork; Krishiv's may not by default. |
| `krishiv.python.worker.tenantMemoryLimit` | size | (none) | cluster | startup | 0.3.0 |  | Address-space limit (`RLIMIT_AS`) of each Python UDF worker of a tenant, when lower than `krishiv.python.worker.memoryLimit`. Unset: the general limit applies. |
| `krishiv.query.maxExecutionTime` | duration | (none) | session | user | 0.2.0 |  | The longest a query may run from the start of its execution: past it the query is cancelled and fails with `KRISHIV_QUERY_TIMEOUT`. The limit is read when the query starts. For a SQL script, the whole script is the query: the limit counts from its start. When unset, queries run without a time limit. |
| `krishiv.query.maxQueuedTime` | duration | (none) | session | user | 0.2.0 |  | Reserved: the longest a query may wait for admission before it starts. No admission queue exists yet, so the value is accepted and has no effect. |
| `krishiv.resultCache.enabled` | bool | `false` | session | user | 0.1.0 |  | Keep the rows of a query for later runs of the same query by any session of the process with the same principal and access-policy version. Only queries over permanent catalog tables with no non-deterministic function are cached. Entries are dropped by `REFRESH TABLE`, `CLEAR CACHE` and every write the engine commits to a table they read; a change made outside the engine is not seen until the entry expires. Off by default. |
| `krishiv.resultCache.maxBytes` | size | `64MB` | cluster | startup | 0.1.0 |  | Most bytes the result cache of an engine runtime holds (the process-wide store of sessions built alone, or a supplied runtime's own), as Arrow batches outside the query memory pool; fixed when the runtime is built. A result larger than the cap is not stored; when a new result would pass the cap the oldest entries go first, and entries past their ttl go whenever a result is stored. Needs `krishiv.resultCache.enabled`. |
| `krishiv.resultCache.ttl` | duration | `1d` | session | admin | 0.1.0 |  | How long the result cache serves an entry, counted from when it was stored; an older entry is dropped before the next lookup and the query runs again. `0s` never expires. Needs `krishiv.resultCache.enabled`. |
| `krishiv.runtimeFilter.adaptive.maxPassPercent` | int | `90` | session | user | 0.1.0 |  | A scan driver stops evaluating a runtime filter on rows once it passes more than this percentage of a measurement window (pruning splits and row groups with it continues). |
| `krishiv.runtimeFilter.adaptive.minRows` | int | `65536` | session | user | 0.1.0 |  | Rows per window over which a scan driver measures a runtime filter's pass rate. |
| `krishiv.runtimeFilter.bloom.atScale` | bool | `true` | session | admin | 0.3.0 |  | A join whose probe-side scan is estimated at least 20 times its build plans its runtime Bloom filter with caps of 20,000,000 keys and 32 MiB instead of `krishiv.runtimeFilter.bloom.maxItems` and `krishiv.runtimeFilter.bloom.maxBytes`, when those are lower (larger builds can get more under `krishiv.runtimeFilter.bloom.memoryTier`). A cap set explicitly still binds unless this key is also set explicitly to true. Results do not change. |
| `krishiv.runtimeFilter.bloom.maxBytes` | size | `8MB` | session | admin | 0.1.0 |  | Largest runtime Bloom filter. A filter capped below its 1% false-positive size is still built unless its expected false-positive rate exceeds 5%. Left at its default, it is raised to 32 MiB for a scan estimated at least 20 times its build (`krishiv.runtimeFilter.bloom.atScale`), and for a build past 20,000,000 keys under a scan 8 times it to 1/64 of the query memory limit (`krishiv.runtimeFilter.bloom.memoryTier`). |
| `krishiv.runtimeFilter.bloom.maxItems` | int | `4000000` | session | admin | 0.1.0 |  | Most build keys a runtime Bloom filter is built for: a build estimated larger plans none, and one that turns out larger publishes none. Left at its default, it is raised to 20,000,000 for a scan estimated at least 20 times its build (`krishiv.runtimeFilter.bloom.atScale`), and for a build past that under a scan 8 times it to the keys the memory tier holds (`krishiv.runtimeFilter.bloom.memoryTier`). |
| `krishiv.runtimeFilter.bloom.memoryTier` | bool | `true` | session | admin | 0.3.0 |  | A join whose build is estimated past the 20,000,000 keys of `krishiv.runtimeFilter.bloom.atScale`, under a probe-side scan estimated at least 8 times it, plans its runtime Bloom filter with a size cap of 1/64 of the query memory limit (`krishiv.memory.limit`, or `krishiv.session.memoryLimit` when lower) and a key cap of the keys that size holds at the filter's false-positive rate. It applies only while `krishiv.runtimeFilter.bloom.atScale` is on. Results do not change. |
| `krishiv.runtimeFilter.bloom.minApplicationRows` | int | `1000000` | session | user | 0.1.0 |  | A runtime Bloom filter is planned only for a scan estimated at this many rows or more (and at least four times the build). |
| `krishiv.runtimeFilter.enabled` | bool | `true` | session | user | 0.1.0 |  | Plan runtime filters: the build side of an inner or left semi hash join publishes the min/max, a small value set or a Bloom filter of its keys to the scans feeding the probe side, which skip splits, row groups and rows no build key can match. Results are the same either way. |
| `krishiv.runtimeFilter.equatedSites` | bool | `true` | session | admin | 0.3.0 |  | A runtime filter on a join key also targets the scans of the columns an inner equi-join below equates with it (a key pair of two plain columns of one type), as on the key's own scan: for `a.k = b.k` below, a filter on `b.k` also filters `a.k` at `a`'s scan. | `krishiv.runtimeFilter.exactSet.maxValues` | int | `4096` | session | admin | 0.1.0 |  | Most distinct build keys a runtime filter tests rows against exactly (a small set or a hash set); with more, a Bloom filter (when planned) or only the min/max range is used on rows. |
| `krishiv.runtimeFilter.inList.maxValues` | int | `50` | session | admin | 0.1.0 |  | Most distinct build keys a runtime filter keeps as a value set; with more, a Bloom filter (when planned) or only the min/max range is published. |
| `krishiv.server.allowCoreDumps` | bool | `false` | cluster | startup | 0.3.0 |  | Whether `krishiv server` may write a core dump. Off by default: a dump holds query data and credentials. |
| `krishiv.server.allowedHosts` | string | `` | cluster | startup | 0.3.0 |  | Comma-separated host names (or IP literals) the admin listener accepts in the `Host` header when it is bound to a loopback address, besides `localhost`, `127.0.0.1` and `[::1]`. | `krishiv.server.metrics.public` | bool | `false` | cluster | startup | 0.3.0 |  | Whether the admin server's `/metrics` answers without the admin token. Only on a loopback address; aggregate counters only. |
| `krishiv.server.readiness.failureThreshold` | positive int | `3` | cluster | startup | 0.3.0 |  | How many consecutive failures of a readiness check make `/readyz` answer 503; one slow moment is not a failure. | `krishiv.server.readiness.interval` | duration | `10s` | cluster | startup | 0.3.0 |  | How often `krishiv server` re-runs its readiness checks (object store, authentication). `/readyz` answers from the last result; a result older than three intervals counts as not ready. |
| `krishiv.server.readiness.required` | string | `` | cluster | startup | 0.3.0 |  | Comma-separated readiness checks that fail `/readyz` when they fail, besides the always required `auth`. Only `auth` is wired today; the warehouse object store check follows. Other checks are reported by the admin API only, because every replica shares them and failing them would remove the whole fleet at once. |
| `krishiv.server.readiness.timeout` | duration | `2s` | cluster | startup | 0.3.0 |  | How long one readiness check may take before it counts as failed. |
| `krishiv.server.shutdownTimeout` | duration | `30s` | cluster | startup | 0.3.0 |  | On SIGTERM or SIGINT, how long running queries may finish before the rest are cancelled (`KRISHIV_QUERY_KILLED`; the drain waits up to 10 more seconds for them to stop). `/readyz` answers 503 and new queries and sessions are refused at once with `KRISHIV_SERVER_DRAINING`; the admin API's `Drain` uses it as its default grace period. | `krishiv.session.memoryLimit` | size | (none) | session | admin | 0.2.0 |  | Memory the queries of one session may hold together: the limit of the session's own pool under the process root (`krishiv.memory.limit` still bounds the process). When unset, a session's queries are bounded by the process limit only. |
| `krishiv.spill.compression` | enum (`lz4`, `zstd`, `none`) | `lz4` | cluster | startup | 0.1.0 |  | Compression of the Arrow IPC buffers in spill files: `lz4` (fastest), `zstd` (smaller files, more CPU) or `none`. Files are self-describing, so the setting only affects files written afterwards. |
| `krishiv.spill.dir` | string | (none) | cluster | startup | 0.1.0 |  | Directory for spill files (operator state written to local disk under memory pressure). | `krishiv.spill.dropBehindBytes` | size | `8MB` | cluster | startup | 0.1.0 |  | How many bytes a spill writer writes before it asks the kernel to write them to disk and drop them from the page cache (Linux). | `krishiv.spill.maxBytes` | size | `64GB` | cluster | startup | 0.1.0 |  | Most bytes spill files may occupy on disk at once, over all queries of the process. A spill that would exceed it fails with `KRISHIV_SPILL_CAP_EXCEEDED`. |
| `krishiv.spill.zstd.level` | int | `1` | cluster | startup | 0.1.0 |  | Zstandard compression level for spill files when `krishiv.spill.compression` is `zstd`: 1 is fastest; higher levels (up to 22) give smaller files and cost more CPU. Levels from -131072 (ultra-fast) are accepted. |

| `krishiv.sql.autoBroadcastJoinThreshold` | signed size | `10485760` | session | admin | 0.1.0 | `spark.sql.autoBroadcastJoinThreshold` | The largest estimated size, in bytes, of a join input that is broadcast to every task without a hint. | `krishiv.sql.collation.schemaLevel.enabled` | bool | `false` | session | user | 0.2.0 | `spark.sql.collation.schemaLevel.enabled` | Whether a schema may have a default collation (`CREATE SCHEMA .. | `krishiv.sql.cteRecursionLevelLimit` | int | `100` | session | admin | 0.1.0 | `spark.sql.cteRecursionLevelLimit` | Most rounds a recursive common table expression may run before the query fails with RECURSION_LEVEL_LIMIT_EXCEEDED; -1 removes the limit. | `krishiv.sql.cteRecursionRowLimit` | int | `1000000` | session | admin | 0.1.0 | `spark.sql.cteRecursionRowLimit` | Most rows a recursive common table expression may produce in all rounds before the query fails with RECURSION_ROW_LIMIT_EXCEEDED; -1 removes the limit. |
| `krishiv.sql.defaultPath` | string | `` | session | user | 0.1.0 | `spark.sql.defaultPath` | What `DEFAULT_PATH` expands to: a comma-separated `SET PATH` element list without `PATH`. Empty means `system.builtin, system.session, current_schema`. |
| `krishiv.sql.execution.arrow.maxRecordsPerBatch` | int | `10000` | session | user | 0.1.0 | `spark.sql.execution.arrow.maxRecordsPerBatch` | Most rows in one Arrow batch handed to a Python UDF; zero or a negative value means no limit (the input batches are passed as they are). |

The page reads the list from `GET /api/internal/embed/config`, which needs no token (the embedded view has no session), so the origins are not secret. Unset, the default, is `'none'`: no page can be framed. Every other page of the UI is never framable. An entry that is not an origin (a path, a wildcard, a quote or a space inside it) makes the server refuse to start. |

| `krishiv.write.idempotencyKey` | string | (none) | session | user | 0.3.0 |  | A key the caller chooses for one logical write. A write whose key is already recorded in the target table's commits (a Delta `txn` action, an Iceberg snapshot summary property, a commit-log entry) writes nothing and succeeds, so a job that retries a statement appends once. The key is scoped to the table. The per-write option of the same name wins over this setting. An empty key is invalid. When unset, writes are not deduplicated across statements. Set it per logical write: while it is set on a session, every later write to the same table with the same key writes nothing. A key lasts as long as the commit that holds it (Delta `txn` retention, Iceberg snapshot expiry, the commit log). Iceberg's writer honours the key, but no SQL or DataFrame write reaches it yet. A directory without a commit log refuses a key. UPDATE, DELETE and MERGE refuse a key set on the session (row-level writes do not take one yet). A writer from before this setting drops the keys of a commit-log checkpoint it writes. |
